title: Isolated Regions

story.briefing: The Core floor plan is a grid of open cells and collapsed ones. Count how many separate open regions remain — a crew cannot walk between two of them.
story.success: Regions counted. The crew knows how many separate teams it needs.

description: Given a grid of 0 (open) and 1 (blocked), count the separate regions of open cells. Two open cells belong to the same region when they touch horizontally or vertically — diagonal contact does not connect them. A grid with no open cells has 0 regions.

examples.explanation: The two open cells touch only at a corner, so they are separate.

hints: Every open cell belongs to exactly one region. Start from an unvisited open cell, mark everything connected to it, and that is one region accounted for.
Explore each region completely before counting the next, and mark cells as you enqueue them rather than as you process them, or the same cell gets queued many times.

Scan every cell. When you find an unvisited open cell, add one to the count and flood outward from it — up, down, left and right — marking every open cell you reach. Use an explicit stack, not recursion; a large region would exhaust the call stack.
